ai.title: Print error from git evals
ai.summary: Adds `console.error` logging for error messages in `run-git-evals.ts`. Logs stack trace and full message object before rejecting. Removes manual stack assignment to error object.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs a background check that pulls answers from other systems, it now prints a clearer notice if something goes wrong: you'll see the full problem and where it happened, instead of just a short error. Who this affects: anyone running internal evaluation checks when a connected system returns an error. What you'd notice: the error log now includes the complete stack trace and message object before stopping the check. This is live today.

ai.title: start-web script now runs start-db first
ai.summary: start-web script updated to bun start-db && bun --cwd web dev. Ensures database initialization before web dev server launch. Scope: package.json scripts.

eli5.text: If you run the command that starts the web development preview, it now automatically starts the database first before launching the preview server. This only affects developers running the web dev environment locally, who will now have their database ready when the preview loads. The change is already live in the main project files.

ai.title: Git evals print completion immediately
ai.summary: run-git-evals.ts prints completion status inside the message handler rather than after Promise.allSettled. Removes the pre-allocated evalRuns array in favor of filtering fulfilled results post-execution. Affects evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts. Logging now occurs per-commit during async execution, decoupling output order from final aggregation.

eli5.text: When the system runs a batch of git repository checks, it now prints a 'completed' message for each one as soon as that check finishes, rather than waiting until every check is done and then listing them all at once. So if you watch the logs, you'll see progress appear live instead of nothing until the end. This affects only the internal tooling that processes these git checks, and it's live today.

ai.title: Add repo name to git eval log
ai.summary: Git eval runner now prefixes `Starting` log line with `testRepoName` variable. Distinguishes evals across multiple repos in parallel runs. Affects `evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts`.

eli5.text: When the system runs an evaluation on a specific commit, the start-up message now includes the name of the repository being tested, making it easier to tell apart simultaneous test runs across different repositories. This is a behind-the-scenes change for internal tooling; if you watched the test output, you'd see the repository name appear in each line like "Starting MyRepo eval 1/5 for commit..." instead of just "Starting eval 1/5 for commit...". It's live and applies to anyone running these internal git-based evaluations.

ai.title: Skip nested repo backup if .git missing
ai.summary: Checkpoint file manager skips nested repos without .git directory. `git rm --cached` wrapped in try-catch to log errors. Prevents crashes during backup of non-git subdirectories.

eli5.text: When backing up a project, the system now skips any subfolder that is not itself a git repository instead of trying to handle it as one. If the system fails to remove a tracked folder while preparing the backup, it records the error and keeps going rather than stopping the backup entirely. This only affects the internal backup process; you would notice it as fewer unexpected interruptions while large projects are being saved, but no new visible feature appears in the app today.

ai.title: Eval runner delays exit by 2s to prevent race conditions
ai.summary: The `run-single-eval-process.ts` script in the `evals/git-evals` directory now delays process termination by 2 seconds using `setTimeout` before calling `process.exit(0)`. This change mitigates race conditions where child processes might not have fully flushed output or completed cleanup tasks before the parent process terminates. The scope is limited to the internal evaluation harness.

eli5.text: When the evaluation system finishes running its tests, it now waits two seconds before fully shutting down. This gives any background tasks a moment to wrap up properly, preventing rare glitches where output could get cut off. You wouldn't see this delay during normal use, but if you were watching internal logs closely, you'd notice the process lingers briefly before reporting completion. The change only affects the internal testing tools, not anything you interact with directly.

ai.title: Version 1.0.325
ai.summary: Internal version bump to 1.0.325 in npm-app/package.json. No functional changes or user-facing features included.

eli5.text: If you use the assistant, the default AI model behind it switched back to the faster, higher-quality option called Sonnet, while the alternative model moved into an experimental section you can opt into. The tool also now keeps a public leaderboard showing how different versions of the assistant performed on standard code tasks, and the automated system that runs and checks those tests got a six-hour timeout so long-running checks don't stall. Internally, the web app now starts its database connection automatically when you launch the development server, and the git-based evaluation runs report their progress, errors, and completion times more clearly. These changes are live today for anyone pulling the latest version.

ai.title: Fix arg list too long in git evals fork
ai.summary: Git evals fork now passes `evalCommit` via temp file path instead of JSON string argument. Prevents `E2BIG` when commit data exceeds OS arg length limits. Affects `evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts` and `run-single-eval-process.ts`. Temp file cleanup runs on child message receipt.

eli5.text: When the system tries to run a code evaluation, it used to pass all the details about which code to test directly in a long command line, which could fail if the details were too big. Now it writes those details to a temporary file and just tells the evaluation process where to find that file instead. If you run git-based evaluations today, they'll no longer crash on large commits.

ai.title: Add result logging to run-single-eval-process
ai.summary: Added console.log for final eval result in run-single-eval-process.ts. Import order for fs adjusted. Improves visibility into eval process outcomes.

eli5.text: When the system runs a single evaluation to check how a feature is performing, it now prints the final result directly to the console so operators can see the outcome without digging through other logs. This is a behind-the-scenes logging add that affects only the internal evaluation tooling team; if you work with those eval scripts, you will now see a line reading the final result appear in the terminal output each time an evaluation finishes. The change is live today and only adds visibility, no workflow or performance behavior changed.

ai.title: Introduce @codebuff/build-tools infisical-run executor
ai.summary: Added `@codebuff/build-tools:infisical-run` Nx executor to standardize Infisical CLI usage across `backend`, `common`, and `evals` project targets. The executor checks for `infisical` availability via `command -v` and falls back to direct execution if missing, removing inline shell conditionals from `package.json` scripts. Updated `backend/project.json`, `common/project.json`, and `evals/project.json` to delegate `start`, `dev`, `db:*`, and `*git-evals` commands to this new executor.

eli5.text: Starting the backend, shared libraries, and evaluation tools now uses a single, consistent way to load sensitive project secrets (through a tool called Infisical), instead of each script repeating that logic inline. The new helper automatically detects whether the secrets tool is installed and, if not, simply runs the code directly so nothing breaks. If you work with these parts of the system, you'll see cleaner, shorter startup commands with one place controlling how secrets and settings are loaded.

ai.title: Cap git evals concurrency to 20
ai.summary: Git evals now limit concurrent processes to 20 via a global `p-limit` instance shared across repositories. `run-eval-set.ts` initializes the limiter, and `run-git-evals.ts` enforces it, replacing previous unbounded parallel execution. Dependency `p-limit` added to `evals/package.json`. This prevents resource exhaustion during large-scale evaluation runs.

eli5.text: When the system runs many evaluation jobs at once, it now caps those jobs at 20 simultaneous processes instead of letting them all start at the same time. This prevents the system from getting overwhelmed and using too many resources when lots of evaluations are triggered. You wouldn't notice anything directly, but the system stays more stable and responsive during busy periods.

ai.title: evals workflow always runs on GH Actions
ai.summary: Removed job-level if condition from .github/workflows/evals.yml, ensuring the workflow triggers on every push. Added a 'Check commit message' step to set should_run_evals output based on [buffbench] presence. Applied conditional execution to all subsequent steps (Setup Bun, Cache, Install, Env, Run evals) to skip heavy operations if flag is false. Adds final 'Workflow completed' step to guarantee job success even when evals are skipped.

eli5.text: The automated evaluation system now starts running on every code change pushed to GitHub, instead of only when a special tag appears in the commit message. The system first checks if the commit message contains the tag '[buffbench]'; if it does, it proceeds to set up the environment and run the full evaluation suite, and if not, it skips those heavy operations. A final step then ensures the whole process completes successfully whether or not evaluations were actually run. This change is live today for all code pushed to the repository.

ai.title: Eval test repo directory naming flattened
ai.summary: Changed `setupTestRepo` in `evals/git-evals/setup-test-repo.ts` to use a flat directory name `${repoName}-${commitSha}` instead of nested `repoName/commitSha`. This simplifies path construction for test repositories. Scope limited to internal eval setup logic.

eli5.text: Test repositories are now stored in flat folders named like 'projectName-commitHash' instead of nested folders where each project had its own subfolder containing commit folders. This makes it easier for the system to locate and manage test repositories during internal evaluation runs. If you were browsing the test directory structure, you'd see simpler, single-level folder names instead of folders within folders. This change only affects internal test setup logic and doesn't impact any user-facing features.

ai.title: Wrap evals.yml conditionals in expression syntax
ai.summary: Updated `if` conditions in `.github/workflows/evals.yml` to use `${{ ... }}` expression syntax. GitHub Actions now requires explicit expression delimiters for step conditionals to prevent parsing ambiguities. Affects CI evaluation pipeline steps including setup, caching, and execution.

eli5.text: The system that automatically tests the code when someone submits a change has been quietly fixed so that it only runs the tests when it's actually supposed to. Engineers who rely on those automated checks will no longer see confusing errors or skipped steps caused by a formatting quirk in how the rules were written. The rules are now written in a way the system fully understands, so the testing process behaves consistently every time. The fix is live today in the automated pipeline that runs behind the scenes.

ai.title: Fix escaped commit message parsing in evals.yml
ai.summary: Refactored commit message check in `.github/workflows/evals.yml` to use environment variable `COMMIT_MESSAGE` instead of direct interpolation `${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}`. Prevents YAML injection and parsing errors from special characters in commit messages. Scope limited to CI workflow evaluation trigger logic.

eli5.text: When a developer writes a commit message with special characters like quotes or brackets, the system now reads that message correctly instead of breaking or misunderstanding it. This fixes a small problem in the automated testing process that runs when code is submitted. If you looked at the logs, you'd see the system properly checks for the trigger word and either runs the evaluations or skips them without errors. This is already live and working today.

ai.title: Limit buffbench concurrency to 10
ai.summary: Reduced global concurrency limit in `evals/git-evals/run-eval-set.ts` from 20 to 10. Call to `setGlobalConcurrencyLimit` updated. Import statements reformatted for readability.

eli5.text: The system now runs at most 10 evaluations at the same time instead of 20. This affects anyone running batches of git repository evaluations through the internal tooling. If you look, you'd see a comment that previously said "20 processes" now says "10 processes," and the import statements are reformatted for readability.

ai.title: evals task dependsOn build-tools:build
ai.summary: Added dependsOn constraint to evals task in evals/project.json. Ensures @codebuff/build-tools:build completes before infisical-run executes run-eval-set.ts. Scope limited to evals project configuration.

eli5.text: When the system runs the evals tests, it now waits for the build tools to finish first before starting the actual evaluation script. This means internal developers will see the evals task pause until the shared code libraries are fully compiled. The change prevents errors that happened when the evaluation code tried to run before the supporting code was ready.

ai.title: Refactor eval model config and add metrics
ai.summary: Eval harness now supports explicit `modelConfig` (agent/reasoning models) passed to `mainPrompt`, overriding default cost-mode selection. `getAgentStream` signature updated to return stream directly, shifting model resolution logic to `common/constants` via new `getModelFromShortName` helper. `GitEvalMetadata` schema extended with `avgCompletion`, `avgEfficiency`, `avgCodeQuality`, `avgDuration`, and `avgTurns` fields. Eval runner aggregates these metrics from trace data before database insertion.

eli5.text: The eval harness now lets the assistant pick a specific AI model for agent and reasoning tasks instead of always falling back to a default cost-based choice, and it records five new average metrics, completion, efficiency, code quality, duration, and turns, in each eval run's report. If you run or review evals, you'll see these averages populated automatically from the run data before they're saved. The change is live today for anyone using the eval tooling, and it doesn't alter the experience for regular users of the product.

ai.summary: In evals/git-evals/run-eval-set.ts, API_BASE now hardcodes http://localhost:3000/. Previous fallback to NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL removed. Scope limited to internal eval runner.

eli5.text: The internal test tool that checks the assistant now always sends its requests to a fixed local address, instead of reading a fallback address from a configuration setting. If you ran these internal tests, you'd see they no longer react to changes in that configuration setting. This only affects the company's own internal testing process, not anything you experience directly.

ai.title: Reorder git checkpoint nested repo handling
ai.summary: The `gitAddAllIgnoringNestedRepos` function in `npm-app/src/checkpoints/file-manager.ts` was refactored to change the execution order of git operations. `gitAddAll` now runs after identifying modified files and removing them from the index, rather than before. This ensures nested repo `.git` directories are backed up and restored correctly relative to the file staging process.

eli5.text: The assistant now saves backups of sub-projects' private folders at the right moment. It first checks which files changed, then backs up any sub-project folders, and finally saves everything. This prevents the backup process from accidentally interfering with the save process. You wouldn't notice anything different unless you were watching the background save-and-backup steps happen.

ai.title: Eval data paths use absolute paths in run-eval-set.ts
ai.summary: Updated `evalDataPath` in `evals/git-evals/run-eval-set.ts` to use `path.join(__dirname, ...)` instead of relative strings. This ensures eval JSON files are resolved correctly regardless of the current working directory when running the script. Scope limited to internal eval runner configuration.

eli5.text: The internal tool that runs automated code evaluations was updated so it can find its test data files no matter where the script is started from. Previously, it looked for those files relative to wherever you happened to be standing when you ran the command, which meant it could fail if you ran it from a different folder. Now it always calculates the correct location based on where the script itself lives, so the evaluation set will run reliably regardless of your starting directory. This is internal maintenance and does not change what any user sees.

ai.title: Pass modelConfig to git evals child process
ai.summary: The `fork` call in `runGitEvals` now serializes `modelConfig` to JSON and passes it as the fifth argument to the child process. This fixes a broken merge by ensuring the eval runner has access to the correct model configuration. The change is isolated to `evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts` and does not affect public APIs or user-facing behavior.

eli5.text: If you ran an automated evaluation of the assistant today, that evaluation was previously starting with a broken or missing model configuration, because the settings describing which model to use were not being handed to the child process that runs the eval. The runner now passes that configuration along, so evals no longer fail or behave inconsistently due to the broken merge. You would have noticed evals producing wrong or missing results without any error message; now they run with the correct model settings as intended. This is live today for anyone running these automated evals.

ai.title: Fix duplicated chat directory in npm-app worker context
ai.summary: Refactored `project-files.ts` to enforce a singleton `currentChatId` and pass this ID to the `project-context.ts` worker via `postMessage`. The worker now calls `setChatIdFromExternal` to align its state with the main thread before processing files. This prevents race conditions where the worker and main thread generated different timestamp-based IDs, causing writes to duplicate chat directories.

eli5.text: Each chat session now uses one shared folder name that both the main app and its background worker agree on, so the app no longer accidentally creates two separate chat folders with slightly different names. You would have noticed duplicate chat folders appearing in your project's chat directory when saving chat context. This fix is live today and affects anyone using the npm-app's chat feature.

This ensures the build-tools executor is compiled before any task attempts to invoke it, preventing race conditions or missing executor errors during Nx task execution.

eli5.text: When you run certain tasks in the system, like starting the backend server or the web app, the system now makes sure a key helper program is fully built and ready before it tries to use it. Previously, the helper program might have been started before it was finished building, causing errors. You wouldn't notice a difference in features, but you should see fewer crashes or errors when starting the system for the first time.

ai.title: Clean up evals console logs

eli5.text: The diagnostic scripts that run internal accuracy tests now print fewer status lines to the terminal, so engineers monitoring those runs see a cleaner, quieter log instead of the previous chatter about how many tests were launching and whether they were running one-by-one. It only affects the behind-the-scenes test tooling used internally, not anything a customer runs.

ai.title: Fix evals git setup to reset repos missing .git directory
ai.summary: setupTestRepo in evals/git-evals/setup-test-repo.ts now checks for .git existence instead of just repoDir. If directory exists but lacks .git, it recursively deletes the folder before cloning. Prevents clone failures when previous runs left partial or corrupted test repos.

eli5.text: When the system sets up a test repo for Git evals, it now checks whether the repo's.git folder exists rather than just the main folder. If the folder exists but lacks.git, meaning a previous run left a partial or corrupted repo, it gets fully deleted before cloning fresh. This prevents failures during setup and keeps Git evals running smoothly today.
